motion_base.note: Take 2 passed 11 of 12 QA rows. The one failure was confined to the head of the clip: Curtis's lips are parted with visible teeth from about frame 5 to frame 40 (0.17-1.63 s). From frame 41 to 121 the mouth is closed, the camera is locked at 1.000x, and every gate row passes.

driving_base.method: Every output frame is a copy of a decoded frame of take 2. Only the ORDER changes. No filtering, no colour work, no scaling, no upscale.

window.method: stream copy from the head of the approved base; every frame bit-exact (frames counted on the uploaded window)

lipsync.loop_mode_note: Never triggers: the 91.458 s driving window exceeds the 90.440 s batch audio.
lipsync.input_retention: fal CDN temporary inputs, 24 h expiry VERIFIED at upload (scripts/fal-upload.mjs)

split.method: Cut at the MIDPOINT of the surrounding silence - 0.24s (10 mp3 frames = 6 video frames) before the narration and the same after it - per the documented split specification, because LatentSync opens the mouth about 6 frames BEFORE the first audible sample. Cutting at the audio onset lands inside that anticipation. Re-encoded at the cut; a stream copy snaps to the nearest keyframe and would desync the remuxed audio. Frame count rounded UP so video always covers the audio.
split.caption_offset_note: Caption cues tile the DELIVERED asset, not the narration. The first cue starts at 0 and the last ends at video_dur_s (15.32s) - which is what the lesson tests assert: captions[0].start === 0, captions.at(-1).end === durationSec, and contiguity between. Do NOT offset cues by the 0.24s lead pad. That silence is INSIDE the asset and therefore inside the first cue; offsetting would push the last cue past the end of the video and fail the test. All three shipped pilots (claims-01, siu-01, ew-01) are authored this way.
split.caption_offset_note_superseded: Cleared 2026-08-21. This sidecar previously carried: 'Caption cues are authored against narration time. This asset begins with 0.24s of silence, so cues must be offset by +0.24s when they are regenerated at Gate D.' That instruction was STALE and would have broken the delivery tests - the shipped cues are not offset and must not be.

audio.note: LatentSync's returned audio (aac 16 kHz) is DISCARDED; the locked 24 kHz -24.5 LUFS master is muxed with -c:a copy, then transcoded ONCE to AAC-LC 128k/24 kHz/mono for delivery. MP3-in-MP4 is signalled as mp4a.69, which WebKit refuses to decode, so the original delivery was silent on Safari and on every browser on iOS. Video stream is COPIED bit-for-bit; nothing was re-rendered and no paid step was repeated. Verified 2026-08-21: frame count, duration, 1920x1080/25 and audio onset all unchanged; loudness held within 0.1 LU.
audio.lufs_measured_over: the narration window only - 0.24s to 0.24s + the narration length. The asset's leading and trailing digital silence is excluded, because including it moves the integrated figure on short segments without touching a single narration sample.
audio.bit_exact_method: containment: the Gate A master's compressed MP3 frame payload appears intact and contiguous inside the delivered payload at byte 3840 (10 silent frames x 384 bytes), which proves both that it was copied and that nothing shifted it

delivery.native: NO upscaling anywhere - the base is native 1920x1080

qa_method: Mouth claims confirmed BY EYE at 2-4x zoom on extracted frames, never from a pixel metric alone (known-mistakes #18). A share-above-luma-150 box calibrated on take 2's known-open frames 5-40 and known-closed frames 41-121 does not separate them for Curtis at all (best gap 0.0000) - his beard and skin tone flatten the contrast the metric needs.

split_rule.what: Segments are cut at the MIDPOINT of the surrounding silence - 0.240 s before the narration and 0.240 s after - instead of at the audio onset.
split_rule.why: LatentSync begins articulating before the sound. Curtis's call 4 measured it: the mouth is already open at return frame 913 while the first audible sample is at frame 919.3, about 6 frames (250 ms) of anticipation. Cutting at the audio onset lands inside that window, so whether a delivered first frame showed closed lips or open teeth depended on the segment's first phoneme.
split_rule.source: This is the split specification already written in docs/VIDEO_1_GENERATION_CONFIGS.md ('cut at the midpoint of each 0.5 s silence... the Selena run measured anticipatory mouth opening 36 ms before speech'). It was not implemented. The 0.640 s batch lead-in added on 2026-08-20 addressed only the batch-OPENING segment and is retained - it also absorbs the model's own 3-frame cold start, which returns an open mouth on frames 0-2 even when the audio is digitally silent.
split_rule.why_0_24: 0.240 s is the only value that is a whole number of both units in play: 10 mp3 frames (24 ms each at 24 kHz) and 6 video frames (40 ms each at 25 fps). It fits inside the 0.5 s inter-segment gap twice with 10 ms to spare, so the approved batch plan is unchanged and NOTHING was regenerated - these assets were re-cut from the returns already paid for, at $0.00.
split_rule.audio_effect: The delivered stream is now 10 silent mp3 frames + the locked master + 10 more, concatenated with -c copy. The master's frames are never re-encoded and its payload is asserted to appear intact and contiguous at byte 3840. Integrated loudness can read up to 0.2 LU from -24.5 because the measurement window now includes digital silence; the narration itself is byte-identical and therefore unchanged.
split_rule.known_scope: Diane's delivered claims-01 set was cut under the old rule and carries open first frames on most of its 22 segments, including `intro` - the frame the start gate holds. FLAGGED, not actioned; her raw returns are not retained, so re-cutting her means re-running her LatentSync calls.

measured.mouth_cheek_reference: Curtis UNTOUCHED base measures 1.646 with identical boxes, so his absolute value is not comparable to Diane (hers sits near 0.85 - a full beard is dense high-frequency texture and loads whichever box holds it). Direction and magnitude are what matter: 1.646 -> this figure is a SOFTENING, the correct direction. Diane v4 softened 0.85 -> 0.74 (-12.9%). The REJECTED demo-driven route inverted UPWARD to 1.10 and read as pasted on.
measured.camera_lock: best-fit zoom vs the approved base frame 1 is 1.000x, 1.000x, 1.000x at start, middle and end - zero drift
measured.background_drift_note: Inside the base's own declared walk (whole-frame drift median 2.103, max 3.384 /255 across its 3410 frames). Isolating the model on the call-6 canary - raw return vs the exact driving window, frame for corresponding frame - gave wall 2.78, window 3.46, desk 2.77-3.22, torso 3.12, eyes 3.77, MOUTH 18.12: the change is 5.8x concentrated in the mouth and uniform elsewhere, the signature of a whole-frame re-encode rather than localised corruption.

lipsync_alignment.method: per-frame mouth activity correlated against the audio envelope across all frames of the batch
lipsync_alignment.note: Peak is one frame from zero - inside EBU R37 (+-40 ms) and well inside ITU-R BT.1359.

measured.first_last_frame_lips_closed: PASS - confirmed by eye at 2-4x zoom on every first and last frame of this call after the re-cut.
